dataset_note: Facts copied from official MSU Billings pages, checked on 2026-10-17. A null field means the data was not found in the source.

credit_system.credit_hour: The credit hour is used as a unit of instruction to quantify student learning; one credit of instruction should be approximated by 45 hours of combined direct instruction (counting a 60-minute class as 1 hour of instruction) and student work. The catalog's Course Terms page adds that MSU Billings requires 37.5 contact hours for a traditional 3-credit class.
credit_system.grading: Letter grades on a 4-point scale (A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, F=0). General Education courses require a C- or better and an overall 2.0 GPA in the General Education core.
credit_system.math_placement: Placement is based on the EdReady initial math placement assessment: the initial score maps to a placement level (e.g., 70+ = Level 45, 55-65 = Level 30, 45 and below = Level 10), and students can raise it by completing the EdReady Study Path. Advisors recommend which math course to register for based on the score (University Campus Advising 406-657-2240).

majors.name: Business Administration Management Option, B.S.
majors.accreditation: Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) - College of Business
majors.description: Offered online. Per the College of Business, business programs at MSU Billings prepare graduates for numerous career paths and leadership roles in business; the Management option focuses on the functions of management, decision making and leading workers. Required math: M 143 Finite Mathematics and STAT 216 Introduction to Statistics, plus quantitative business courses such as BGEN 240.
majors.career_outcomes: Business programs at MSU Billings prepare graduates for numerous career paths and leadership roles in business, enabling graduates to immediately engage as productive members of local, regional, and global economic and social systems.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take BGEN 105A Introduction to Business in the first fall semester to see if business fits you.

majors.name: Psychology, B.S.
majors.college: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
majors.description: Per the department, a bachelor's degree in Psychology can serve as a general liberal arts degree, as preparation for a career in psychology, or as preparation for graduate school; students design and execute research and complete supervised work in a professional setting. Required math: a General Education math course (STAT 141 or STAT 216) plus PSYX 222 Psychological Statistics, and a 6-8 credit Mathematics/Computer Science or Language option.
majors.career_outcomes: Psychology majors develop excellent interpersonal, research, writing, and analytical skills and are attractive to a wide variety of employers; to prepare for a psychology career with a bachelor's degree, students are encouraged to consult faculty and complete internships in the Billings community, and those planning graduate study should get a broad background in psychology and a high GPA.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take PSYX 100 Intro to Psychology in the first fall semester (a grade of C or higher is required in major psychology courses).

majors.name: Broadfield Major in Elementary Education, B.S.Ed.
majors.department: Department of Educational Theory and Practice
majors.accreditation: Educator preparation programs accredited by CAEP (Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation); all programs that include educator licensure are accredited by the Montana Board of Public Education.
majors.description: The College of Education provides an array of undergraduate programs for educator preparation; this major prepares students to create inclusive, culturally responsive K-8 classrooms and design student-centered instruction, ending with a full semester of student teaching. Required math: M 130 Math for Elementary Teachers I and M 131 Math for Elementary Teacher II, plus EDU 397C Methods: K-8 Mathematics.
majors.career_outcomes: The catalog has no career-outcomes section for this major. The College of Education describes it as educator preparation; licensure requires student teaching and a qualifying Praxis Subject Assessment score, with applications approved by the college's Licensure Specialist before going to the state licensure office.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take EDU 105 Education and Democracy in the first fall semester to see if teaching fits you.

majors.name: Health Administration, B.S.
majors.department: Department of Health Sciences and Human Performance
majors.college: College of Health Professions and Science
majors.description: Offered online. Per the catalog, Health Administration is one of the fastest growing professions in the United States, and the program is designed to meet the rapidly evolving demands of a dynamic industry; it requires an internship. Required math: STAT 216 Introduction to Statistics, plus accounting (ACTG 201, ACTG 202) and economics (ECNS 201) in the business core.
majors.career_outcomes: Careers in health administration include a wide range of management and administrative positions in hospitals, ambulatory care, physician group practices, laboratories, pharmacies, social service agencies, long-term care facilities, rehabilitation centers, home health organizations, managed care plans, regulatory agencies, and health insurance companies.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take HTH 270 Global Health Issues in the first spring semester, then HADM 305 Survey of US Healthcare System in year two.

majors.name: Communication, B.A.
majors.college: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
majors.description: Offered online. The B.A. in Communication examines mediated, organizational, and public relations communication processes through theoretical grounding and applied knowledge, teaching writing, speaking, and critical thinking skills with internship opportunities. Required math: no math beyond the 3-credit General Education mathematics requirement; the major requires an 8-credit modern language requirement.
majors.career_outcomes: The degree is designed to prepare students to serve as public communication professionals within corporate, non-profit, government, healthcare, and education settings, and provides excellent preparation for graduate study in communication as well as law.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take COMX 111 Intro to Public Speaking (recommended General Education communication course) in the first fall, then COMX 300 Exploring Comm Studies in year two.
